A<sup>xially</sup> <sup>chiral</sup> <sup>compounds</sup> <sup>have</sup> <sup>received</sup> <sup>significant</sup>
attention from both synthetic and medicinal communities
due to their widespread presence in natural products, chiral
ligands, and catalysts.<sup>1</sup> Among these, the catalytical enantio-
selective synthesis of (hetero)aryl-based C−X (X = C, O, N, B,
etc.) atropisomers<sup>2</sup> and allene-based atropisomers<sup>3</sup> has been a
hot topic in the synthetic community over the past few decades
(Scheme 1a). In comparison, the enantioselective synthesis of
axially chiral alkylidenecycloalkanes remains in its infancy due
to the challenge arising from the longer distance between the
four groups about the chirality axis. At present, the majority of
methodologies to access enantioenriched axially chiral
alkylidenecycloalkanes focuses on the noncatalytic strategy,
i.e., with the aid of stoichiometric chiral reagents.<sup>4</sup> The
catalytic methods in this area have been somewhat limited,<sup>5</sup>
including enantioselective olefination of 4-substituted cyclo
hexanones and their analogs,<sup>6</sup> desymmetrization of 4-
substituted cyclohexanes and derivatives,<sup>7</sup> [2 + 2] cyclo-
addition between terminal alkenes and allenes,<sup>8</sup> and deracem-
ization of racemic alkylidenecycloalkanes<sup>9</sup> (Scheme 1b). In
view of the remarkable roles of axially chiral alkylidenecy-
cloalkanes in bioactive molecules and chiroptical molecular
switches as well as chiral ligands (Scheme 1c),<sup>10</sup> further
development of novel methods for synthesizing these
architectures is still highly desirable.
α-Allenols make up a crucial class of allenes that possess a
1,2-propadiene moiety and a hydroxyl group. Due to their π-
activated reactivity, α-allenols and their derivatives have found
extensive applications in organic synthesis,<sup>11</sup> and various
fascinating transformations have been well-established, where-
into, transition-metal catalyzed C1-allylic substitution has
emerged as a general strategy to construct allenes bearing a
central chirality,<sup>12</sup> or chiral allenes<sup>13</sup> (Scheme 2a, upper panel).
When the external nucleophiles attack the C3-position of 2,3-
allenol and analogues via transition-metal catalysis, achiral
multiply substituted 1,3-dienes would be generated (Scheme
2a, bottom panel).<sup>14</sup> However, to the best of our knowledge,
the enantioselective construction of axially chiral alkylidenecy-
cloalkanes using α-allenols and their derivatives remains
unknown. We hypothesized that by rational design of allenol
derivatives and precise control of the regioselectivity, it would
be possible to generate axially chiral alkylidenecycloalkanes by
enantioselective C3-substitution.<sup>15</sup> Building upon our research
interests in transition-metal-catalyzed enantioselective desym-
metrization and atroposelective construction of axially chiral
compounds,<sup>16</sup> we present herein a copper-catalyzed enantio-
selective allenylic substitution of acyl 2,3-allenols (Scheme 2b).
With phenylsilane used as the hydride donor, the axially chiral
alkylidenecycloalkanes containing a 1,3-dienyl motif are
constructed in good yields with excellent enantioselectivities.
In addition, copper-catalyzed enantioselective silylation and
borylation could also proceed, giving products containing
functionalized dienyl motifs.

In summary, we have developed a copper-catalyzed
enantioselective synthesis of axially chiral alkylidenecycloal-
kanes with acyl 2,3-allenols. This reaction features broad
substrate scope, mild conditions, and excellent regio- and
enantioselectivities. Control experiments show that the choice
of acyl group is important to both the yield and
enantioselectivity. The terminal alkene and vinyl boronate
motifs of the products could participate in a series of
downstream transformations. Further application of this
catalytic strategy to the enantioselective synthesis of function-
alized axially chiral alkylidenecycloalkanes is ongoing in our
laboratory.
